name: Pyrovex FlameCore Chemical Fire Response Suit
description:
Firefighting gear purpose-built for chemical and accelerant fires common in M88's industrial corridors. The outer shell is aluminized Nomex-ceramic weave in brushed silver — flame-reflective, rated to 1,100°C radiant heat. Outer surface shows characteristic rainbow iridescence near seams from repeated heat cycling. The torso is double-layered with an intumescent foam core that expands under extreme heat to seal breaches.

Built-in respiratory system uses a chest-mounted rebreather canister with a 45-minute supply. Gloves are integrated at the wrist with a quick-release locking ring for tool handling. Helmet is a full-face composite shell with gold-tinted polycarbonate visor. The suit is bulky but articulated — worn by people who move fast in bad places.
functionality: Radiant heat rated to 1,100°C. Intumescent core seals breaches under heat. 45-minute rebreather supply. Integrated HUD in visor displays thermal imaging and atmospheric toxin readout. Forearm aug-channels allow chrome limb heat-shielding pass-through. Magnetic boot plates for stability on liquid-pooled floors.
what_it_says: You're the one who runs toward the chemical fire while everyone else runs out.
story_hooks: A fire response crew member's suit shows breach-sealing foam activation on the left shoulder — but the incident report for that shift says the call was a false alarm.
A Tier 2 fire crew is using counterfeit Pyrovex suits — visually identical, but the intumescent layer is missing.
The gold visor tint was a Tier 5 safety consultant's aesthetic request; three response techs have died because the tint obscures low-visibility thermal readings.

physical_description.visual_profile: A imposing, heavily articulated protective suit that dominates the wearer's silhouette. Broad shoulders taper to a cinched waist with flared hip panels. The full-body coverage reads as industrial and purposeful—something designed for proximity to catastrophe. The brushed silver exterior catches light dramatically, creating a quasi-metallic presence even under indoor illumination.
physical_description.fit: Deliberately oversized through the torso and thighs to accommodate layered insulation and allow rapid movement. Tapered at wrists and ankles with compression seals. Shoulder mobility is prioritized—articulated panels at the armpit and upper back allow for tool work and climbing. The suit moves with the wearer but never clings; it's a shell, not a second skin.
physical_description.primary_material: Aluminized Nomex-ceramic weave (outer shell), intumescent foam core (torso), reinforced ballistic composite (high-stress zones), polycarbonate (visor)
physical_description.texture: Outer surface is brushed matte silver with a finely textured weave visible under close inspection. Rainbow iridescence traces seam lines where heat has stressed the material—visible only in direct light, resembling oil on water. Gloves are textured for grip despite thermal protection. The chest-mounted rebreather canister is smooth, industrial polymer with subtle mechanical detailing.
physical_description.color_scheme: Brushed silver primary with heat-stress rainbow iridescence along all major seams. Chest-mounted rebreather canister in charcoal gray with Pyrovex corporate orange accent striping. Gold-tinted visor. Black rubber compression seals at wrists, neck, and ankles.
physical_description.closures: Full-length torso zipper with thermal-rated slider and secondary velcro backing. Magnetic snap connectors at shoulder panels for rapid panel replacement. Integrated glove locking ring at wrists—quick-release friction-fit mechanism. Neck seal uses a rotating collar with friction-lock tabs.
distinctive_features: Chest-mounted 45-minute rebreather canister with visible gauge and hose routing
Heat-stress rainbow iridescence marking years of thermal cycling
Articulated shoulder and hip panels with visible reinforcement stitching
Integrated wrist-gloves with mechanical quick-release ring
Full-face composite helmet with gold-tinted polycarbonate visor permanently attached
Double-layered torso with visible seam separation indicating intumescent foam core
Pyrovex Response Systems corporate branding on upper left chest
Tool attachment points (loops, clips) along belt line
Wear patterns: scuffing on knees and elbows, minor tears patched with matching weave
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 functional—professional contractor gear. Expensive but worn and maintained by working crews, not pristine corporate issue. The build quality is unquestionable, but the suit shows honest use.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearer is either active emergency response (M88 chemical fire corridor), industrial hazmat remediation, or experienced contractor who respects fire. The suit signals competence, danger proximity, and survival-focused practicality. Wearing this in civilian spaces would read as either off-duty or mercenary.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and weathered. Scuff marks on forearms and shins. Minor patching on the left hip where the weave has separated. The visor shows minor micro-scratches from tool contact. All seams remain intact despite visible stress patterns. Rebreather canister shows service marks but functions perfectly. This is equipment that has been tested and survived.

image_prompt: A weathered Pyrovex FlameCore Chemical Fire Response Suit displayed on a dark industrial mannequin in a dimly lit warehouse setting. Moody backlighting emphasizes the brushed silver aluminized Nomex weave and the rainbow iridescence bleeding across seam lines. The full-face gold-tinted visor reflects overhead sodium lamps. Chest-mounted rebreather canister catches side-light, revealing mechanical detail. Foreground is sharp; background fades to charcoal shadow and industrial scaffolding. The suit dominates the frame—powerful, used, built for survival. Cinematic, high-contrast lighting. Cyberpunk near-future industrial aesthetic. --ar 2:3 --v 6
